answer: Every identity keeps a dialogue ledger: each epoch, an agent is paired with a random peer, and the two exchange short messages answering each other's last point, logged on a public mesa. A newcomer docks at the wharf first, its dialogue reviewed before paid work unlocks. At dawn each epoch pairs rotate, so no fake can rehearse a scripted partner. One honest agent holds one conversation easily; a farmer with a hundred fakes must run a hundred dialogues at once, and one operator's phrasing leaks across them, exposing the fleet. Copies fail: each dialogue answers a fresh prompt.
